validity.recommendation: Keep the row. Existence, gas-transmission classification, endpoints, fuel source, 16-in diameter, 100 MMcf/d capacity and operating status are all independently corroborated.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — REAL. Two independent outlets confirm the line: (1) MEES 2024-05-24 states 'the oil ministry completed a 1km, 16-inch spur connection to an existing gas line linking Jambur oil field to Kirkuk, to bring the earmarked 100mn cfd'; (2) KirkukNow 69751 reports the Ministry of Oil / North Gas Company + North Oil Company completed the Khor Mor (Chamchamal, Sulaymaniyah) -> Jambur (Kirkuk) dry-gas line to feed the Kirkuk (Taza district) gas power station, completed 5 Nov 2023; KirkukNow 70189 corroborates (existing Khor Mor->Jambur line dating to 1980s, renovated, plus new Jambur->Kirkuk-power-plant branch, 100 MMcf/d). CLASSIFICATION — correct: dry natural-gas transmission line feeding a power station, not gathering/plant-internal, not an oil/NGL line. NB the GulfPub oil roster has a separate 'Jumboor - Kirkuk' line (12-in CRUDE, Jumboor field -> Kirkuk refinery, OPC) — different commodity and endpoint, NOT this row. DUPLICATE — none. Distinct from P6823 (Khormor-Pirdawood, Khor Mor -> Erbil, 24-in, 180 km) which serves the Kurdistan/Erbil side; P6827 serves the federal Kirkuk/Taza power station. ATTRIBUTION — operator is the Iraqi state (Oil Pipelines Company / North Gas Company / North Oil Company); Khor Mor field operated by Pearl Petroleum (Dana Gas/Crescent consortium). FuelSource = Khor Mor field: confirmed. Start province Sulaymaniyah/Chamchamal, end Kirkuk: confirmed. SPEC — all confirmed vs sources: diameter 16 in (MEES explicit '16-inch'); capacity 100 MMcf/d (MEES + both KirkukNow articles); length 1.05 km / 1,050 m (MEES '1km spur'); dates StartYear1 1980 (existing 1980s Jambur-Kirkuk line) + StartYear2 2023 (new spur, completed Nov 2023). REF-QUALITY notes for a human: (a) Status [ref] kirkuknow/69751 fails an 'operating' token check only because the article says 'completed' (semantically = operating); it does support the status. (b) Length [ref] currently points to the iraqieconomists PDF which does NOT contain '1.05' — replace with MEES, which states the 1km spur explicitly.

validity.recommendation: Clarify what LengthKnown represents. The 1.05 km reflects ONLY the 2023 spur, not the full Khor Mor->Jambur->Kirkuk corridor implied by the name (~50 km field-to-power-station).
validity.researcher_notes: The row name 'Khor Mor-Jambur-Kirkuk Gas Pipeline' implies the full supply corridor, but LengthKnown=1.05 km is only the new 16-in spur completed 2023 (MEES: '1km, 16-inch spur connection to an existing gas line linking Jambur oil field to Kirkuk'). GEM's own Background note already flags this ('the diameter... refers to the added one km only, in 2023. I assumed the rest of the pipeline might have the same diameter'). This is a modeling/scope caveat, not a data error: the 1.05 km is correctly the sourced spur length. No source gives a full end-to-end length for the combined 1980s line + 2023 spur; straight-line Khor Mor(35.13N,44.85E) to Kirkuk/Taza(~35.3N,44.35E) is ~50 km. Human decision: keep 1.05 km as the new-build spur length (recommended, since that is what is sourced) OR relabel/split. Not an existence or classification doubt.

routes.corridor_desc: The gas-supply corridor runs WNW from the Khor Mor field (Chamchamal district, Sulaymaniyah governorate) across the Kirkuk governorate boundary to the Jambur field/station SE of Kirkuk, then to the Kirkuk (Taza district) gas power station. Physically two parts: an older (1980s) Jambur->Kirkuk gas line that was renovated, plus a new 1.05 km / 16-in spur completed Nov 2023 connecting Khor Mor into the existing Jambur-Kirkuk line. Straight-line Khor Mor->Taza is ~50 km; the entered 1.05 km is only the new spur. Endpoints are firmly named and sourced; the exact routing between them is not mapped, so the corridor is bounded loosely (a broad SE-Kirkuk-to-Khor Mor band via Jambur).
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints and the Jambur waypoint are named directly by KirkukNow 69751 (Khor Mor/Chamchamal -> Jambur -> Taza/Kirkuk power station) and MEES (Jambur oil field -> Kirkuk). Coordinates: Khor Mor field 35.135N,44.855E (sourced via field-profile/Wikidata search; ~50 km SE of Kirkuk); Jambur field 35.317N,44.479E (approximate centroid of the 35-km anticline SE of Kirkuk, from Iraqi Geological Journal descriptions); Kirkuk/Taza power station 35.30N,44.34E is APPROXIMATE, defensible from the Taza Khurmatu locality ~20 km S of Kirkuk — treat end coord as loosely bounded. No coordinate fabricated; the end-point coord is flagged approximate rather than left null because the named locality (Taza) is well established.

summary: P6827 Khormor-Jambur-Kirkuk gas line CONFIRMED (caveat): real, correctly classified gas transmission, not a duplicate; 16-in/100 MMcf/d/1.05 km all corroborated — caveat is that 1.05 km is only the 2023 spur, not the full corridor.
